claims.text: This trip was billed on an upfront quote and that fixes which clause governs the money. fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is 34.50, so POL-RD-11 applies and POL-RD-02 does not run: the rider is not entitled to a distance-or-time refund on the excess however large it is, because those charges were fixed at booking. The rider's advocate does not press the extra-distance limb of the claim. What remains live is the comparison POL-RD-11(a) itself directs - charged_total against quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 - and the pass-through correction POL-RD-11(b) preserves.

Run the POL-RD-11(a) comparison and the recoverable sum falls out. Charged_total is 39.00 and quoted_fare_sgd is 34.50, an excess of 4.50 over the quote; but only 2.50 of that excess is a properly chargeable pass-through - the KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) ERP of 2.50, which lies on the optimal route (trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd is 2.50, and optimal_route_source records the optimal route as KPE then CTE then SLE, crossing the Defu Flyover gantry only). The remaining 2.00 is the AYE gantry line, which has no chargeable basis on this trip. On the clause's own arithmetic quoted 34.50 + chargeable pass-through 2.50 = 37.00, and 39.00 exceeds that by 2.00, which is refunded in full.

The 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line is a charge for a gantry this vehicle never passed, and the fare_breakdown's own proximity block says so: the nearest fix to that gantry is 5,419.29 m away - the first fix of the trace at 21:10:00 - and the line carries on_optimal_route false. The trace never comes within the 250 m radius POL-RD-09(4) uses to treat a fix as a crossing, so the line has no counterpart anywhere in the trace or the trip record. That is a billing-integrity failure, and POL-RD-09(4) makes it refundable in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The driver's own denial that he went near an AYE gantry is consistent with the trace and confirms the line is not a crossing at all.

The rider is not overreaching and says so: she does not seek the KPE (Defu Flyover) 2.50 back. The trace passes within 44.50 m of that gantry, well inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09(4) applies, the line carries on_optimal_route true, and the optimal route crosses that gantry. It is a properly chargeable pass-through and is correctly left out of the correction. What is left after removing the one unmatched line is 2.00, and that is the whole of what is asked.

The deviation is established on the figure POL-RD-01 says governs. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 28.18 against an optimal_distance_km of 22.40, an excess of 5.78 km, which is 25.80% of optimal - above both POL-RD-01 gates, the more-than-20% test and the more-than-0.8 km test - and the derived deviation block records status 'established' with the trace figure, not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 28.2, which POL-RD-01 forbids citing for the threshold test. That matters here because the driver's account of his own route change is on the record: he wrote in the chat log that CTE was heavy and that he went KPE then TPE, which is not the recorded optimal corridor of KPE then CTE then SLE.

The driver's traffic explanation buys him nothing because the only advisory artifact in the bundle is MISSING. EV-ADVIS-00115-01 carries no payload at all and therefore weight 0.0: no advisory names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, no validity window overlaps the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached the affected segment, and no shortest-lawful-alternative distance exists to run the POL-RD-03 cap on. POL-RD-03 exoneration therefore cannot be run at all, and the artifact is cited here for its absence, which is itself a citable fact. Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden of pointing to a specific artifact and a specific clause.

Nor can the driver move the excess onto the rider. POL-RD-04 requires an instruction that comes from the rider and identifies a place or road specifically enough to act on, such as a named road to take. The only two messages on the trip are the driver's 'CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE' at 21:14:10 and the rider's one-word 'ok' at 21:14:50. The rider named no road and gave no waypoint - waypoint_hint is null on both messages - so the corroboration test cannot be run and, on the clause's own terms, POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record. That also means POL-RD-09(3), which bars an ERP refund only where the detour was rider-caused under POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12, is not engaged.

The counterparty's answer that 'she paid the quote' is contradicted by the ledger it points to. fare_breakdown records payment_status CHARGED with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50 and total_charged 39.00 - an excess of 4.50 over the quote - and the quote therefore did not absorb what was charged. On the POL-RD-11(a) test the rider was charged 2.00 more than the quote plus the one properly chargeable gantry, and that 2.00 is refunded in full.

This case is ready for a monetary ruling and no POL-RD-10 trigger fires. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown - TRP-00115 appears on all three - so limb (2) is not engaged; the trace is unimpaired on its face, with coverage_pct 100.0, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0.0 and a 10-second sampling interval against an expected interval of 10 seconds, so neither POL-RD-07 nor limb (3) is engaged; and the only charge line with no counterpart in the trace is the AYE gantry, which is refunded under POL-RD-09(4) and is expressly carved out of limb (8) by that limb's own proviso. The record settles the money question, so holding the amount back on an escalation would serve no one.

The rider carries her POL-RD-08 burden on this record and no extra corroboration is demanded of her. Limb (a) is satisfied by the matching trip identifiers and pickup timestamps across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and limb (b) by the 25.80% excess measured from a trace that is unimpaired under POL-RD-07. The extra-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 applies only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer; here both are 0, so it does not bite. Those are the only profile fields the clause names, and POL-GEN-01 confines every other field on either profile to credibility context and nothing more.

The rider does not seek a repeat-deviation uplift and none is available on this record, which is why the claim is confined to the pass-through correction. A 25.80% excess and 5.78 km fall below the 50% and 8.0 km thresholds that would make this a MATERIAL deviation under POL-RD-01 and trigger the POL-RD-06 profile check; and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 523 satisfies neither limb of POL-RD-06's pattern test (not 3 or more, and not 0.05 or more against a base of at least 40). POL-RD-06's near-synonym prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is not the trailing-90-day figure the clause asks for, so it cannot be substituted.

The outcome the evidence supports is PARTIAL_REFUND of 2.00 - the whole of the contested AYE line, refunded in full under POL-RD-11(a) read with POL-RD-09(4), which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis so it is not a NO_ACTION case, and far below 90% of charged_total so it is not a FULL_REFUND either. Under POL-GEN-03 that is a partial return of the contested amount to the filing party, and it is accompanied by a POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral for the unmatched gantry - a referral only, which under POL-GEN-03 adds to the ruling and does not replace it or hold the money back.

claims.text: The rider's distance claim fails at the outset. fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is 34.50, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking; POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront-quoted trip and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess. The detour cost her nothing on those lines, and there is no distance money to give back.

The burden of proof does not change that answer. POL-RD-08 expressly lists POL-RD-11 among the clauses the driver may point to in answering the rider's prima facie case, and the driver invokes it here: charged_total of 39.00 is exactly the 34.50 quoted fare plus 4.50 of ERP lines, so not a cent of distance or time charge moved and none can be recomputed against the driver.

Even taking the platform's own measurement at its highest - a trace distance of 28.18 km against a booked optimal of 22.4 km, an excess of 5.78 km or 25.8% - any deviation established under POL-RD-01 is not a MATERIAL one: it falls below both the 50% and the 8.0 km thresholds, so POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not triggered and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral can follow from it.

Even if POL-RD-06 were consulted, no repeat-deviation pattern exists. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the 3 the clause requires, and 1 against completed_trips_90d of 523 is 0.0019, far below the 0.05 ratio. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a deliberate near-synonym and is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 names; under POL-GEN-01 it is context only and may never ground a finding against the driver.

The 2.50 KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) line stands and the rider must bear it. The booked optimal route itself crosses that gantry - the trip record's optimal_route_source describes the optimal as crossing the Defu Flyover gantry only - and the driver's trace passes within 44.5 m of it at 21:32:40, well inside POL-RD-09's 250 m crossing radius. It is a gantry actually crossed on the optimal route, so it is a properly chargeable pass-through.

The driver does not resist the 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line, and the record shows why it cannot be his. The trace's closest approach to that gantry is 5,419.3 m, far outside the 250 m match radius, and the gantry is not on the optimal route. It is a billing-integrity defect refundable in full under POL-RD-09(4) and recorded as a referral - a platform billing error, not driver misconduct, and the driver takes no benefit from it. It is also the ceiling of this dispute: 2.00, not the 6.00 contested.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and the case should be decided on its merits rather than held. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (100% coverage, 229 fixes at a 10 s interval, no gaps, maximum gap 0 s), so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; no timestamps run backwards; and the only charge line with no counterpart in the trace is the AYE line, which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes because POL-RD-09(4) refunds it.

The driver disclosed the reroute as it happened and did not take it behind the rider's back: he messaged her at 21:14:10, 'CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE', and she replied 'ok' at 21:14:50. The rider's 'ok' does not satisfy POL-RD-04 - the clause requires an instruction from the rider identifying a place or road, and waypoint_hint is null - so no exoneration is claimed on it; but the exchange is why the fare she now disputes was the flat quote from the moment she accepted it.

Candour: no traffic advisory covers this trip. EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is MISSING - its payload is null and it carries weight 0.0 - so the driver does not assert POL-RD-03 exoneration, and a general assertion that CTE was heavy, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, cannot discharge the burden under POL-RD-08. I state this plainly rather than stretch it, but nothing turns on it: because the fare was upfront, the distance charge is fixed under POL-RD-11 and neither exoneration nor its absence moves a dollar.

ruling.explanation: To both parties. The disputed trip TRP-00115 ran on 8 Aug 2026 from Marina Bay Financial Centre to Woodlands, and the money question turns on how it was priced, not on how it was driven. EV-FARE-00115 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50 and total_charged 39.00. On an upfront-quoted trip POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run: the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so no distance-or-time refund is available however large the detour. The extra-distance half of the rider's claim is therefore not payable. For completeness, the deviation is established under POL-RD-01 on the governing trace figure (EV-GPS-00115 trace_distance_km 28.18 against booked optimal 22.40, an excess of 5.78 km / 25.8%, clearing both the 20% and 0.8 km gates), but it is not MATERIAL (below 50% and 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not triggered, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 523 establishes no pattern in any event, and the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01. No repeat-deviation uplift and no driver-conduct referral arise. Neither party disputed any of this, and the driver's candour that no traffic advisory covers the trip is noted: EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is empty (weight 0.0) and no POL-RD-03 exoneration was asserted, so nothing turns on it under an upfront fare. That is a billing-integrity failure, and POL-RD-09(4) makes it refundable in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The driver's own denial that he went near an AYE gantry is consistent with the trace and confirms the line is not a crossing at all.

The rider is not overreaching and says so: she does not seek the KPE (Defu Flyover) 2.50 back. The trace passes within 44.50 m of that gantry, well inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09(4) applies, the line carries on_optimal_route true, and the optimal route crosses that gantry. It is a properly chargeable pass-through and is correctly left out of the correction. What is left after removing the one unmatched line is 2.00, and that is the whole of what is asked.

The deviation is established on the figure POL-RD-01 says governs. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 28.18 against an optimal_distance_km of 22.40, an excess of 5.78 km, which is 25.80% of optimal - above both POL-RD-01 gates, the more-than-20% test and the more-than-0.8 km test - and the derived deviation block records status 'established' with the trace figure, not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 28.2, which POL-RD-01 forbids citing for the threshold test. That matters here because the driver's account of his own route change is on the record: he wrote in the chat log that CTE was heavy and that he went KPE then TPE, which is not the recorded optimal corridor of KPE then CTE then SLE.

The driver's traffic explanation buys him nothing because the only advisory artifact in the bundle is MISSING. EV-ADVIS-00115-01 carries no payload at all and therefore weight 0.0: no advisory names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, no validity window overlaps the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached the affected segment, and no shortest-lawful-alternative distance exists to run the POL-RD-03 cap on. POL-RD-03 exoneration therefore cannot be run at all, and the artifact is cited here for its absence, which is itself a citable fact. Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden of pointing to a specific artifact and a specific clause.

Nor can the driver move the excess onto the rider. POL-RD-04 requires an instruction that comes from the rider and identifies a place or road specifically enough to act on, such as a named road to take. The only two messages on the trip are the driver's 'CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE' at 21:14:10 and the rider's one-word 'ok' at 21:14:50. The rider named no road and gave no waypoint - waypoint_hint is null on both messages - so the corroboration test cannot be run and, on the clause's own terms, POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record. That also means POL-RD-09(3), which bars an ERP refund only where the detour was rider-caused under POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12, is not engaged.

The counterparty's answer that 'she paid the quote' is contradicted by the ledger it points to. fare_breakdown records payment_status CHARGED with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50 and total_charged 39.00 - an excess of 4.50 over the quote - and the quote therefore did not absorb what was charged. On the POL-RD-11(a) test the rider was charged 2.00 more than the quote plus the one properly chargeable gantry, and that 2.00 is refunded in full.

This case is ready for a monetary ruling and no POL-RD-10 trigger fires. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown - TRP-00115 appears on all three - so limb (2) is not engaged; the trace is unimpaired on its face, with coverage_pct 100.0, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0.0 and a 10-second sampling interval against an expected interval of 10 seconds, so neither POL-RD-07 nor limb (3) is engaged; and the only charge line with no counterpart in the trace is the AYE gantry, which is refunded under POL-RD-09(4) and is expressly carved out of limb (8) by that limb's own proviso. The record settles the money question, so holding the amount back on an escalation would serve no one.

The rider carries her POL-RD-08 burden on this record and no extra corroboration is demanded of her. Limb (a) is satisfied by the matching trip identifiers and pickup timestamps across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and limb (b) by the 25.80% excess measured from a trace that is unimpaired under POL-RD-07. The extra-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 applies only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer; here both are 0, so it does not bite. Those are the only profile fields the clause names, and POL-GEN-01 confines every other field on either profile to credibility context and nothing more.

The rider does not seek a repeat-deviation uplift and none is available on this record, which is why the claim is confined to the pass-through correction. A 25.80% excess and 5.78 km fall below the 50% and 8.0 km thresholds that would make this a MATERIAL deviation under POL-RD-01 and trigger the POL-RD-06 profile check; and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 523 satisfies neither limb of POL-RD-06's pattern test (not 3 or more, and not 0.05 or more against a base of at least 40). POL-RD-06's near-synonym prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is not the trailing-90-day figure the clause asks for, so it cannot be substituted.

Under POL-GEN-03 that is a partial return of the contested amount to the filing party, and it is accompanied by a POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral for the unmatched gantry - a referral only, which under POL-GEN-03 adds to the ruling and does not replace it or hold the money back.

The rider's distance claim fails at the outset. fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is 34.50, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking; POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront-quoted trip and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess. The detour cost her nothing on those lines, and there is no distance money to give back.

The burden of proof does not change that answer. POL-RD-08 expressly lists POL-RD-11 among the clauses the driver may point to in answering the rider's prima facie case, and the driver invokes it here: charged_total of 39.00 is exactly the 34.50 quoted fare plus 4.50 of ERP lines, so not a cent of distance or time charge moved and none can be recomputed against the driver.

Even taking the platform's own measurement at its highest - a trace distance of 28.18 km against a booked optimal of 22.4 km, an excess of 5.78 km or 25.8% - any deviation established under POL-RD-01 is not a MATERIAL one: it falls below both the 50% and the 8.0 km thresholds, so POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not triggered and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral can follow from it.

Even if POL-RD-06 were consulted, no repeat-deviation pattern exists. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the 3 the clause requires, and 1 against completed_trips_90d of 523 is 0.0019, far below the 0.05 ratio. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a deliberate near-synonym and is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 names; under POL-GEN-01 it is context only and may never ground a finding against the driver.

ledger.claim: The 2.50 KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) line stands and the rider must bear it. The booked optimal route itself crosses that gantry - the trip record's optimal_route_source describes the optimal as crossing the Defu Flyover gantry only - and the driver's trace passes within 44.5 m of it at 21:32:40, well inside POL-RD-09's 250 m crossing radius. It is a gantry actually crossed on the optimal route, so it is a properly chargeable pass-through.

The driver does not resist the 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line, and the record shows why it cannot be his. The trace's closest approach to that gantry is 5,419.3 m, far outside the 250 m match radius, and the gantry is not on the optimal route. It is a billing-integrity defect refundable in full under POL-RD-09(4) and recorded as a referral - a platform billing error, not driver misconduct, and the driver takes no benefit from it. It is also the ceiling of this dispute: 2.00, not the 6.00 contested.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and the case should be decided on its merits rather than held. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (100% coverage, 229 fixes at a 10 s interval, no gaps, maximum gap 0 s), so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; no timestamps run backwards; and the only charge line with no counterpart in the trace is the AYE line, which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes because POL-RD-09(4) refunds it.

The driver disclosed the reroute as it happened and did not take it behind the rider's back: he messaged her at 21:14:10, 'CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE', and she replied 'ok' at 21:14:50. The rider's 'ok' does not satisfy POL-RD-04 - the clause requires an instruction from the rider identifying a place or road, and waypoint_hint is null - so no exoneration is claimed on it; but the exchange is why the fare she now disputes was the flat quote from the moment she accepted it.

Candour: no traffic advisory covers this trip. EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is MISSING - its payload is null and it carries weight 0.0 - so the driver does not assert POL-RD-03 exoneration, and a general assertion that CTE was heavy, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, cannot discharge the burden under POL-RD-08. I state this plainly rather than stretch it, but nothing turns on it: because the fare was upfront, the distance charge is fixed under POL-RD-11 and neither exoneration nor its absence moves a dollar.
